title: What agentic AI actually is (and isn't): a builder's definition
openingParagraph: 79% of companies say they've adopted AI agents. Only 1 in 9 runs them in production. (Accelirate, June 2026.) That gap is not a technology problem. It is a definition problem — and in banking and payments, that definition gap is now a regulatory exposure.
linkedinPost:
79% of companies claim AI agents in financial services. Only 1 in 9 runs them in production.

The gap is not a technology problem. It is a definition problem — and in banking and payments, that gap is now a regulatory exposure.

What I would actually do right now as a COO in a regulated financial institution:

- Map every AI agent claim against a 5-level autonomy axis — most are Level 3 workflows, not Level 4 agents
- Define the human gate before scoping the agent (KYC: PEP match; credit: exposure threshold)
- Build the EU AI Act audit registry into the architecture from day one — retrofitting costs 3x more
- Start with one high-volume narrow task (AML triage, credit memo, regulatory report) before deploying broadly

The EU AI Act takes effect August 2, 2026. Only 21% of companies have mature oversight for autonomous agents.

Full piece + the 5-level autonomy axis framework I use when scoping agent deployments — link in comments.
